# Sort

## Summary
The shared sort verb: one type-aware comparator so every list orders the same way. `sortBy(items, accessor, direction)` sorts stably; `compareValues` compares numbers numerically, Dates by time, strings with numeric-aware locale rules ("2" before "10"), booleans false-first. The two rules apps kept getting wrong are pinned: null/undefined/empty sort LAST in either direction (an unfilled field never floats to the top because the column flipped), and ties keep incoming order so a secondary sort survives. Holes in the item list (unloaded links) are skipped, not crashed on.

## Usage
```ts
import sortBy from './utils/sort';

let byDue = sortBy(tasks, (t) => t.dueDate, 'asc');      // undated tasks last
let byPriority = sortBy(byDue, (t) => priorityRank(PriorityField, t.priority));
```
Four shipped apps re-derived per-column sorting before this existed (the second-highest demand count on the P1 list); the Table block's `sortValue` columns are the natural feed.

## Non-goals
Not a query: server-side ordering belongs to the search index's `sort` expressions — this is for lists already in hand. No natural-language collation options beyond locale defaults; a consumer with a bespoke collation passes a pre-computed sort key through the accessor instead.
